text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal continued his rich vein of form to challenge strongly in the English Open on Thursday, increasing Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros' hope that his compatriot will soon seal his Valderrama place.

In 29 rounds since returning from an 18-month layoff with foot problems, Olazabal is a remarkable 76-under-par. His three-under-par 69 on Thursday, to lie three strokes off Englishman Roger Chapman's early first round lead, kept the Spaniard in with a fine chance of virtually making sure of his Cup place in only seven events of his comeback.
Only a bogey on his last hole and another disappointing display with the driver prevented Olazabal being even closer to the lead.
If he were to collect the 108,330 pounds ($177,000) first prize and its equivalent Ryder Cup points, Olazabal's Valderrama spot would be a formality, earning him his second win of the season.

"To win I've got to hit the ball better off the tee," said the 31-year-old Spaniard, who will have his first lesson for two years from his English coach, former Ryder Cup captain John Jacobs, next week at the European PGA Championship.
"The rest of my game is okay but I'm beginning to believe there isn't a driver in the world which can make me hit the ball straight off the tee."

Chapman, 37, is looking to be the bride instead of the bridesmaid this time. The English Open is just one event he has lost at the death in a 16-year career which has brought six second places on the European Tour and 11 worldwide. He has been in the European Tour's 'Millionaire Club' for some time but is the only player in the select group who has never won.
An accomplished 66 took him into the early lead, one ahead of Germany's Thomas Goegele.

"I could have won this event a few years ago but bogeyed the last two holes," said Chapman, who has taken on a new sports psychologist to help him overcome winner's nerves. "And that's been the story often. Now I feel I can enjoy the closing stretch for the first time in my life, so I'm hopeful of my first win."
